title: Using Synthetic Biology to Engineer Living Cells That Interface with Programmable Materials
protocol: Mix 25 g of LB powder stock with 1 L of deionized (DI) water.
Autoclave the solution at 121 °C for 20 min to sterilize.
Add 15 g agar to the LB media before autoclaving to prepare LB plates.
Wait until the sterilized LB media's temperature is below 60 °C and then add 1 µL of antibiotic stock for every 1 mL of LB media if preparing media with an antibiotic.
Prepare a separate stock solution of 5X M9 salts at 56.4 g/L.
Prepare a separate stock solution of 1 M MgSO4.
Prepare a separate stock solution of 1 M CaCl2.
Prepare a separate stock solution of 20% glucose.
Prepare a separate stock solution of 2% biotin-free casamino acids.
Combine 20 mL of 5x M9 salts, 200 µL of 1M MgSO4, 10 µL of 1 M CaCl2, 2 mL of 20% glucose, 1 mL of 2% biotin-free casamino acids, and 76.8 mL of DI water in an autoclave safe bottle.
Autoclave the solution at 121 °C for 20 min.
Incubate cultures at 37 °C with agitation at 400 rpm.
Vary incubation times depending on experiment and strain, typically lasting from 8 to 12 h.
Grow E. coli MG 1655WT cells overnight at 37 °C.
Combine 1 µL of the overnight culture with 9 µL of sterile DI water in a PCR tube.
Incubate the tube at 95 °C for 5 min.
Transfer the tube to a -80 °C freezer for 10 min to lyse the cells.

Thaw the solution and add 2.5 µL each of primers nBioB2-f1 and nBioB2-r, 5 µL of 5x DNA polymerase buffer, 0.25 µL of DNA polymerase, 0.5 µL of dNTP mix, and 6.75 µL of DI water for a total reaction volume of 25 µL.
Strike the tube to mix its contents.
Spin down the tube quickly (~ 2 s) to ensure the sample is at the bottom of the tube.
Place the tube in a PCR thermocycler.
Use the program described in Table 3 with an additional step of 3 min at 95 °C at the beginning of the protocol.
Confirm successful PCR using gel electrophoresis (1.0 - 1.2% agarose in DI water + ethidium bromide) in Tris base, acetic acid, and EDTA buffer (TAE).
Extract DNA fragments from gel from step 2.1.7 using commercial kits according to manufacturer's instructions.
Isolate the Ptrc-2 promoter and the lacI operon from the plasmid pKDL07113.
Grow E. coli cells containing the pKDL071 plasmid overnight in LB + Cb at 37 °C.
Extract the plasmid DNA from the cells using a commercial miniprep kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Replace lysed cells with the plasmid extract in step 2.2.2.
Use 2.5 µL each of primers 1-f and 1-r for lacI cassette extraction.
Alternately, use 2.5 µL each of primers nBioB1-f and nBioB1-r for Ptrc-2 extraction.
Perform gel electrophoresis (step 2.1.7) to confirm the PCR products are the lacI cassette and Ptrc-2 promoter site.
Confirm the lacI cassette is 1213 bp long.
Confirm the Ptrc-2 promoter site is 109 bp long.
Use splicing by overlap extension (SOE) PCR to build the bioB cassette containing Ptrc-2, a synthetic ribosome binding site (RBS), and the bioB gene.
Digest pKE1-MCS plasmid vector with restriction enzymes AatII and EcoRI for the lacI cassette.
Digest pKE1-MCS plasmid vector with restriction enzymes HindIII and SacII for the bioB cassette.
Incubate digestion reactions at 37°C for 1 hour after assembly.
Prepare gels for electrophoresis according to standard protocols.
Combine digested DNA with gel electrophoresis 6x loading buffer.
Use a 2-log ladder to verify location of desired construct.
Cut DNA fragment from the gel.
Extract DNA fragments from the gel using commercial gel extraction kits.
Quantify extracted DNA using spectroscopy.
Mix ligation reaction by combining 1 µL 10X Ligase Buffer, 1 µL T4 Ligase, 50 ng vector DNA, a specific mass of insert DNA, and DI water to reach a total reaction volume of 10 µL.
Incubate the ligation mixture at room temperature for 1 hour.
Aliquot 1 mL of overnight cultures into 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 16,200 x g for 1 minute.
Decant the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 200 µL chilled (on ice) 100 mM CaCl2.
Resuspend the pellet gently by pipetting without vortexing. Place the tube on ice for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge again, remove the supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 100 µL chilled 100 mM CaCl2. Place the tube back on ice.
Centrifuge a final time, resuspend the pellet in 50 µL chilled 100 mM CaCl2, place the tube on ice, and use immediately.
Add 5 µL of ligated DNA to each tube containing competent cells.
Agitate briefly by flicking the tubes and place them on ice for 30 minutes.
Heat shock the tubes for 45 s at 42 °C.
Return the tubes to ice for 2 min.
Pipette cells onto selective LB agar + antibiotic plates.
Spread the cells using glass plating beads.
Incubate the plates overnight at 37 °C.
Pick colonies from insert-positive plates (i.e., 1:1 and 3:1 plates) in the morning.
Pick 3 colonies if the 0:1 negative control plate shows no growth, or pick 5-8 colonies if there is some growth on the 0:1 plate.
Inoculate 5 mL LB + antibiotic with the picked colonies and grow for 8 h at 37 °C with agitation.
Extract plasmid DNA from the cells using a miniprep kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Perform a test cut using restriction enzymes following the procedure detailed in step 2.4.1.
Identify cells with successful constructs by comparing digested DNA fragment lengths to expected results from correct constructs.
Mix equal parts of culture with sterile-filtered, 40% glycerol (in DI water) for preservation.
Freeze the mixture at -80 °C for long-term storage.
Grow engineered strains overnight in LB media with an appropriate antibiotic.
Prepare 50 mL of minimal M9 media without DTB and IPTG.
Inoculate the prepared media with overnight culture at a 1:100 dilution.
Aliquot 200 μL of culture in triplicate to each well in a 96-well plate.
Measure OD600 every 5 min over 24 h with continuous shaking and incubation at 37 °C in a plate reader.
Replace the bioB gene in pKE1-lacI-bioB with mCherry for real-time optical quantification.
Add varying amounts of IPTG ranging from 0.1 mM to 5 mM to induce expression in LB media.
Inoculate supplemented, biotin-free minimal M9 media with overnight culture at a 1:100 dilution.
Incubate the cultures and measure fluorescence every 30 min for 15 h.
Grow pKE1-lacI-bioB in E. coli MG1655 strain overnight in LB media.
Supplement M9 media with DTB ranging from 30 to 200 ng/mL.
Add 0.5 mM IPTG to induce biotin synthesis.
Inoculate supplemented, biotin-free minimal M9 media with overnight culture at a 1:100 dilution.
After 24 h of growth, centrifuge cells and collect the biotin-enriched supernatant.
Measure biotin-enriched supernatant with the indirect control and the direct control functionalized surfaces.
Use the supernatant in place of the biotin sample in steps 5.23 and 6.12, respectively.
Prepare an SMCC solution consisting of 20 mg/mL of succinimidyl trans-4-(maleimidylmethyl) cyclohexane-1-carboxylate (SMCC) in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Prepare an SPDP solution consisting of 20 mg/mL of succinimidyl 3-(2-pyridyldithio) propionate (SPDP) in DMSO.
Add 1.4 µL of the SPDP solution to 20 µL SA solution.
Incubate the solution from step 5.2 for 1.5 h at room temperature, wrapped in aluminum foil to avoid exposure to light.
Add 2.4 μL of DDT solution to the solution from step 5.3 and incubate for 1 h at room temperature.
Mix 7.5 μL SMCC solution with 72 μL HRP solution and incubate for 1.5 h at room temperature, wrapped in aluminum foil to avoid exposure to light.
Mix 17 μL LC-LC-biotin solution with 200 μL BSA solution and incubate for 1.5 h at room temperature, wrapped in aluminum foil to avoid exposure to light.
Centrifuge the solutions from step 5.4 at 10,000 x g until the tube volume reaches 100 µL or for 16 min.
Fill the spin tube with 400 μL PBS-EDTA and repeat centrifugation five times.
Store the stock solution at 4 °C after final concentration reduction.
Centrifuge the solutions from step 5.5 at 10,000 x g until the volume reaches 25 µL or for 16 min.
Fill the spin tube with 475 μL PBS and repeat centrifugation five times.
Store the stock solution at 4 °C after final concentration reduction.
Centrifuge the solutions from step 5.6 at 10,000 x g until the volume reaches 100 µL or for 12 min.
Fill the spin tube with 400 μL PBS and repeat centrifugation five times.
Repeat steps four times.
Centrifuge at 10,000 x g until volume reaches 100 µL or for 12 min.
Add 100 µL of PBS to the tube.
Store stock at 4 °C.
Mix 25 µL of 10 mg/mL HRP solution with 25 µL of 10 mg/mL SA solution.
Store mixture at 4 °C overnight.
Prepare a 1:4 working solution from the overnight mixture.
Store in 4 °C fridge.
Store remaining solution at -20 °C.
Mix 10 µL of BSA-biotin stock with 490 µL of PBS.
Incubate plate containing 100 µL of step 5.12 solution at 37 °C for 1 h, wrapped in foil.
Wash the wells of the plate with 0.05% Tween 80.
Add 200 µL of 0.05% PBS-Tween 80 to the wells.
Incubate for 2 min at room temperature (RT).
Decant the liquid.
Repeat step washing three times.
Add 100 µL of the 0.5% casein solution to each well in the 96-well plate.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C for 1 h.
Wash the wells three times with 0.05% Tween 80.
Prepare a solution by mixing 12 mL of 0.5% casein solution with 7.5 µL of 0.05% Tween 80.
Dilute SA-HRP stock 1:10,000 using the prepared solution in step 5.19.
Add 80 µL of the diluted solution to each well of a 96-well plate.
Add 20 µL of the biotin sample to each well of the polystyrene plate.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C for 1 h.
Wash the wells three times.
Mix 50 mM sodium acetate solution, 1 % TMB solution, and 3% H2O2 solution at a ratio of 1,000:10:1 (total volume of 20 mL).
Add 200 µL of the mixed solution to each well.
Allow the mixture in each well to sit for 15 min at room temperature under foil cover.
Add 50 µL of 2 M H2SO4 to each well to stop the reaction.
Measure OD450 using a plate reader.
Prepare 20 mg/mL LC-LC-biotin in DMSO.
Prepare 10 mg/mL HRP in PBS.
Prepare 0.17 µg/mL SA in PBS.
Prepare 0.5% casein in PBS.
Prepare 20% Tween 80 stock in DI water.
Prepare 0.05% Tween 80 (from 20% stock) in PBS.
Prepare 50 mM of sodium acetate in DI water.
Prepare 1% TMB in DMSO.
Prepare 3% H2O2 in DI water.
Prepare 2 M H2SO4 in DI water.
Add 7.5 µL LC-LC-biotin to 72 µL HRP and incubate at room temperature for 1.5 h, wrapped in aluminum foil.
Transfer the solution from step 6.2 to a centrifugal concentrator within a spin tube.
Centrifuge the solution at 10,000 x g until the volume reaches 100 µL or for 12 min.
Fill the spin tube to 500 µL with PBS and repeat the centrifugation and PBS addition four times.
Store the stock at 4 °C.
Add 100 μL of SA solution to each well in a 96-well polystyrene plate.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 1 hour, wrapped in foil.
Wash the wells with 0.05% Tween 80.
Add 200 μL of 0.05% Tween 80 to each well.
Incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature (RT).
Decant the liquid from the wells.
Repeat steps involving washing three times using 0.05% Tween 80.
Add 200 μL of 0.5% casein solution to each well in the plate.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 1 hour.
Wash the wells three times as previously described.
Dilute the biotin-HRP stock 1:10,000 using the solution prepared earlier.
Add 80 μL of diluted biotin-HRP to each well in a new 96-well plate.
Add 20 μL of the prepared biotin sample to each well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 1 hour.
Wash the wells three times as previously described.
Mix 50 mM sodium acetate, 1% TMB, and 3% H2O2 in a ratio of 1000:10:1 (total volume of 20 mL).
Add 200 μL of the mixed solution to each well and incubate for 15 minutes at RT covered with foil.
Add 50 μL of 2 M H2SO4 to each well to stop the reaction.
Measure OD450 using a plate reader.
